#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The `validateJobsPodsStatusOnlyWithTimeout` function causes fatal errors when the client fails to obtain Job objects even once. However, there are some situations where the client fails due to rate limiter restrictions, not timeouts like this test case:

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/120586/pull-kubernetes-integration/1828447614387884032
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-integration/1828481333362429952

```shell
job_test.go:3973: Failed to get updated Job: client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context deadline exceeded
I0827 15:47:15.178118  112969 job_controller.go:239] "Shutting down job controller"
```

So, this PR allows us to retry polling until a specified timeout.

Thank you for letting me know.
I will try to investigate the root cause of the flaky case.

@alculquicondor It seems that this failure is not related to the test case. It looks like test infrastructure limitations.
What do you think?
Maybe it's a sign that we are putting too short of a deadline somewhere?

> https://testgrid.k8s.io/presubmits-kubernetes-blocking#pull-kubernetes-integration

I think so too. Actually, we can see the same error in [TestBackoffLimitPerIndex/job_index_fails_due_to_exceeding_the_global_backoff_limit_first](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/directory/pull-kubernetes-integration/1828481333362429952) as well.

So I would propose increasing timeout here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3cb89ebb08e8c28eb3a3dc4baeb3a5117dbbea0/test/integration/job/job_test.go#L4356

@alculquicondor WDYT?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3cb89ebb08e8c28eb3a3dc4baeb3a5117dbbea0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/config.go#L130-L131

> I don't think that would help:
> 
> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3cb89ebb08e8c28eb3a3dc4baeb3a5117dbbea0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/config.go#L130-L131

That makes sense. In that case, can we output the log and retry the listing instead of disrupting polling there?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/de6db3ffb0680f2022f8795038eb2ca5b36c5bd6/test/integration/job/job_test.go#L3972-L3974
The root cause is disrupting the polling if the listing fails even once.
I see, yeah. But I wonder if the `ctx` passed to `PollUntilContextTimeout` contains any additional timeout. Maybe not.

> I see, yeah. But I wonder if the `ctx` passed to `PollUntilContextTimeout` contains any additional timeout. Maybe not.

It seems that we received dedicated timeout as a last arg and then set the timeout to `PollUntilContextTimeout` like this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/de6db3ffb0680f2022f8795038eb2ca5b36c5bd6/test/integration/job/job_test.go#L3967-L3970

So, I think that it looks better to retry the listing until reaching the polling deadline.

Throughout more investigation, it seems that the `PollUntilContextTimeout` returns err immediately once the condition func returns err there:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e5bafe2bed13fe72e88a3597930bdfbab5267e9d/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/loop.go#L50-L57

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e5bafe2bed13fe72e88a3597930bdfbab5267e9d/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait/loop.go#L85-L90

> ```diff
> 	if err := wait.PollUntilContextTimeout(ctx, waitInterval, timeout, true, func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
> 		updatedJob, err := clientSet.BatchV1().Jobs(jobObj.Namespace).Get(ctx, jobObj.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
> 		if err != nil {
> +			t.Logf("Failed to get updated Job: %v", err)
> +			return false, err
> - 			t.Fatalf("Failed to get updated Job: %v", err)
> 		}
> ``` 

So, instead of my proposal above, we need to ignore errors like the following. This will not cause another flaky test since we always verify the expected and actual Job there:

```diff
	if err := wait.PollUntilContextTimeout(ctx, waitInterval, timeout, true, func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
		updatedJob, err := clientSet.BatchV1().Jobs(jobObj.Namespace).Get(ctx, jobObj.Name, metav1.GetOptions{})
		if err != nil {
+			t.Logf("Failed to get updated Job: %v", err)
+			return false, nil
- 			t.Fatalf("Failed to get updated Job: %v", err)
		}
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/de6db3ffb0680f2022f8795038eb2ca5b36c5bd6/test/integration/job/job_test.go#L3983-L3986

I simulated the error situation in my local like this:


review_comments: Yes, that is potentially the same problem. But, I have never seen the flake test. So, I would like to ask @alculquicondor @mimowo if we should apply the same approach to other places at Job integration tests so that we can resolve potential issues.

Actually, there are even more functions which use `PollUntilContextTimeout` for Jobs:  `validateJobCondition`, `waitForPodsToBeActive`. We also use this pattern directly in `TestElasticIndexedJob`. I think the reason that `validateJobsPodsStatusOnlyWithTimeout` failed is just how timing / order of tests plays out. 

IIUC any request (GET / PATCH / LIST ...) may result in the error. This suggests to me we should bump the QPS / Burst params. I can see these are set to some very high numbers in some tests, examples: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c86a2d6925a61ac181468b74f573518db1d645d2/test/integration/kubelet/watch_manager_test.go#L46-L47
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c86a2d6925a61ac181468b74f573518db1d645d2/test/integration/volume/attach_detach_test.go#L331-L332
If we don't want to bump the QPS I would suggest to apply this approach to all functions using `PollUntilContextTimeout` sending requests to Jobs.

TBH, I'm ok with either approach (QPS vs retry).
But, I guess that the QPS approach does not resolve the root cause.
Because this may happen again once the QPS in other testing for other SIGs are increased higher than Job integrations, right?
IIUC we have client configuration scoped to the Job tests: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c86a2d6925a61ac181468b74f573518db1d645d2/test/integration/job/job_test.go#L4354-L4355.

Yes, that's true.
I wanted to say the situations where we increase the client QPS to 1000001, and then if the kubelet testing increases QPS to 1000002. In that case, we may face the same problem. WDYT?
The integration tests create separate clients and API servers per test, so I don't see how they could influence each other.

> The integration tests create separate clients and API servers per test, so I don't see how they could influence each other.

Oh, I did not know that. So, we can take either approach.
Thanks!

We can probably do both.

But for this change, there are certain scenarios where it doesn't make sense to retry and just fail, like when the job doesn't exist. But maybe we don't need to over optimize, as we expect the test to succeed.

/lgtm
/approve

> We can probably do both.

That makes sense. In that case, I will try to open a PR to increase QPS and Burst parameters. 

> But for this change, there are certain scenarios where it doesn't make sense to retry and just fail, like when the job doesn't exist. But maybe we don't need to over optimize, as we expect the test to succeed.

That is a good point; I think that we may want to raise errors when the polling fits NotFound error, but I believe that we can introduce the optimization after we observe any testing problems.
